card.name: Water quality and pollution in state waters
card.fires_on: Small words and punctuation, often the possessive 's after a state name, inside text about water pollution, nutrient limits and coastal or shellfish waters.

modes.label: Possessive after a state
modes.description: The 's after a state or place name just before waters, rivers or similar water terms.
modes.example: EPA approved FDEP’s revised rules to reduce nutrient pollution in Florida<<’s>> treasured waters.

modes.label: Linking words in water lists
modes.description: Commas, prepositions or the start of an acronym in lists of water bodies and water-protection rules.
modes.example: the numeric limits for nitrogen and phosphorus in springs<<,>> lakes and streams (outside South Florida)

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning fresh, so it pushes away "fresh" as the next word in water-related text.
card.plain: It fires on small words in environmental writing about state waters, where the next word is likely a water term rather than "fresh".
